[quote=versia;58986978][i]Marcus nodded. "My Lord, I'm not trying to say our nation is comparable to yours. That is far from the truth. If that were so, I would not be summoned here. So you are right, perhaps we [b]are[/b] alike in many ways. Speaking of such..." Marcus would pull out his telegram from the Rex. "I bring a message from my sovereign Rex. He extends his warmest regards and has entrusted me to speak on his behalf." The telegram consisted of this;

"Glorious Jarl Freyderic and esteemed rulers of Jomsland, I am Rex Lucianus Honorius Maximus Vers Reyvers XIV of Vers. May Jupiter smile upon you and bless you. I bring to you Legatus Marcus Junius Silvanus, an Officer of high status within my royal army, to establish trade, or to form an alliance whether it be military or economic. I understand that a diplomat would be far more suitable for such negotiations, but seeing the terrorism from the notorious Sal-Baliz worries and troubles my spirit. Legatus Marcus will speak on my behalf and for all of Vers. He brings with him his Legion as his personal guard, should he be attacked. My only wishes are to establish cordial ties with you and your people, to prosper both our regions, and to protect the fragile peace within Elseyr by any means necessary. May good fortune and peace follow you for the rest of your days. 

Signed,
Rex Lucianus Honorius Maximus Vers Reyvers XIV of Vers"
[/i][/quote]
Jarl Freyderic sat beside the Legatus in one of the SUVs, his keen eyes studying the man as he retrieved a telegram bearing the seal of the Rex. The Jarl remained silent as Marcus read the message, his expression unreadable. Only once the words had settled did he give a small nod, his fingers idly tracing the engravings of the wolfs head on his belt.
"Your sovereign honors us with his words, and we welcome his goodwill," he said, looking up at Marcus. "It is no small thing to send a warrior instead of a diplomat. It tells me that your Rex values strength and trust in equal measure."
As the convoy passed through the gates of Bondahall, warriors of the Jomsviking Order stood at attention, their long cloaks billowing in the cold wind. Some wore modern combat gear, others the battle-worn armor of their ancestors, but all carried the same unwavering discipline in their stance. Stepping out of the vehicle, Jarl Freyderic turned to Marcus, his coat shifting in the cold northern breeze. Before them loomed Bondahall, a towering fortress of dark timber and stone, its high roof carved with ancient runes. Two great iron braziers flanked the entrance, their flames crackling against the twilight. Warriors lined the steps, clad in chain and leather, their rifles slung beside their broad axes. Their expressions were unreadable, but their presence alone spoke volumes,this was a land where strength was not only valued but expected.
At the bottom of the steps was him, High King Jorik III. Of Jomsland. His piercing blue eyes, glimmering with both sharp wit and amusement, studied the Versian Legatus. Despite his relatively young age, Jorik carried an aura of ancient power. Unlike his warriors, Jorik was supporting himself on a cane.
At first, he said nothing, letting the silence stretch between them as his gaze flicked over Marcus and his legionaries. Finally, a smile, one that could mean many things, spread across his lips.
"So," he mused, his voice smooth yet edged with something dangerous. "The mighty Rex of Vers sends not a diplomat, but a warrior. A man of deeds, not words. That I can respect.But before we speak of war and treaties, let us do what warriors do best,drink, feast, and then we can speak of diplomacy."
He gestured toward the great doors of the hall, which groaned open to reveal the flickering glow of torchlight and the deep roar of voices within. The scent of roasted meat, ale, and woodsmoke spilled into the cold evening air. Inside, long tables stretched beneath wooden beams carved with the sagas of Jomslands greatest heroes. Mead-horns clashed, laughter mixed with the sharp ring of steel as warriors playfully tested each others strength, and the fires burned bright.
Jorik stood, leaning slightly on his cane as he descended the steps. Despite his slight limp, his legs twisted from birth, it did not hinder him. There was no weakness in his stride, only the confidence of a man who had never allowed fate to dictate his strength. He stopped before Marcus, tilting his head slightly.
"Tell me, Legatus," he said, his grin sharpening, "can a Versian hold his drink?"

[b]Directorate of State Security Headquarters, March 31st, 2025, 16:00[/b]

What was meant to be a routine inspection for the Cybersecurity Office, a subdivision for State Security, took a turn for the worst.
As supervisor Janković orders his team to begin a security scan on files from ministries and government-adjacent agencies, one of the technicians would alarmingly raise his hand.

[i]"Sir!"[/i], a young lad would yell, half stood up from his seat. [i]"A-a file belonging to the Ministry of Transportation, relating to the railway transporting of state resource has been remotely accessed!"[/i]

[i]"WHAT?!"[/i] snaps a jolted Janković, yet, with a hint of dismay in his voice. [i]"From where? Where was this file accessed from?!"[/i]

[i]"Uhhhh... Let me check... the access logs... aaaaaand..."[/i], after a brief minute, the young technician would produce results. [i]"Got it! It looks like it came from.. from the town of Ribvenj..? Looks like the exact IP traces to an old derelict factory."[/i]

[i]"Transportation doesn't have an office building in Ribvenj, and certainly not some old factory that's about to fall apart. I'll notify the Deputy Director, and have a SAJ unit raid the building."[/i]
As Janković is walking to his office, another technician raises his hand, and speaks out.

[i]"Sir! Files belonging to the Ministry of Armaments was just remotely accessed from the town of Koplovak! Files accessed range from inventory of weapons being transported and time schedules."[/i]

[i]"Sir files from... from us were accessed 20 minutes ago. Accessed files are uhhh... are the entire roster for the Office of Cybersecurity... The files were accessed from what appears to be an apartment complex in Etrovski."[/i]

Janković begins to slowly turn around in disbelief, his face aghast with the realisation that the whole office has their hands raised, trying to alert their supervisor that more and more files have been remotely accessed at some point during the day. The office erupts into an incoherent mess.

[b]The Raid, various locations, March 31st, 2025, 16:24[/b]
Some time after the office chaos, members of the police special unit, Special Anti-Terrorist Unit (or SAJ), are quickly called to mobilise. Several squads would be needed for this.
Dawning their equipment of helmets, body armour, ammo pouches, face covering masks, the whole shebang, all in a stylish black colour scheme, and armed with a variety of SMGs, shotguns, and sidearms, the 8 squads all mount up on their respective vehicles, ranging from simple vans, to even modified Mil Mi-17 helicopters, with their armaments removed.

As each team arrived on site, they would bust open the doors of their vans, repelled from their transport helicopters, and breached the doors leading to the source, they found little in evidence of the culprits. Some sites had food cans, or wrappers, that were recently opened. Normally, this could indicate a homeless presence.
The raid on the apartment complex in Etrovski, however, went differently. As the SAJ team broke down the door, and breached and cleared the apartment they noticed the window leading to the emergency escape stairs opened. As one of the officers peaked out, he noticed a hooded figure bolting down the stairs. The officer quickly bolts down after him, alerting the rest of his team, causing the SAJ commander to call in patrol officer assistance, hoping to cut him off.
Unfortunately for law enforcement, however, the chase proved fruitless, and the hooded figure escaped. Though, there is light at the darkness. The team is able to secure the apartment building, and all the evidence, mainly the culprits still active laptop, it holds. With hope, the lead won't go cold.

[b]Palata Slavarija, Slakovets, April 1st, 10:45[/b]
The following day, having learned of what transpired yesterday, the National Authority meets in the government building, the Palace of Slavaryia, to discuss the breach in national security.
Each minister would stand by their seat until the Premier, along with his vice, would sit. Once the Premier had his fun, by making the ministers stand a little longer than they'd like, would sit, and the rest of the room would follow.

Ivan Stanković, the Minister of Defence, would look particularly distressed.
[i]"Unacceptable. This simply cannot stand. If the rest of Elseyr found out about this breach in security.. We'll be a laughing stock. An easy target."[/i] 

[i]"He's quite right, sir."[/i] chimes in the Minister of Foreign affairs, Savatije Aleksić, looking towards the Premier. [i]"Given our governments ideological stance, and policies, it'll be hard enough to maintain cordial relations with our neighbours, never mind the more belligerent nations, that will simply use our ideology as a pretence to justify war against us."[/i]

[i]"Our defences may be compromised. We can't guarantee if our missile defence or radar systems wont be rendered inoperable, in the event of foreign invasion."[/i] Minister Stanković turns his attention to the Minister of Internal Affairs, Stanoje Zorić.
[i]"Minister Zorić, has State Security been able to identify who these blatant terrorists are?"[/i]

[i]"Unfortunately, it is too early to produce results. As a matter of fact, it may take a while. The apartment complex that the SAJ team raided, in Etrovski, has been sealed off to the public, and I have a specialist team, from State Security, investigating it. We've also recovered a laptop, but I'm hesitant to have State Security dig around in it."[/i]

[i]"Well why the hell not?!"[/i] barks Minister Stanković, [i]"You have a perfectly good lead, and you choose no-[/i]

[i]"Because, frankly, I have absolutely NO trust in our cybersecurity division!"[/i] a, now, furious Zorić retorts, putting the rest of the room to silence.
[i]"The fact that this group, of whoever-the-hell-they-are, was able to hack into classified government, and military, documents is a glowing testament to how poorly our cyber defences are! For all we know, this group could be a rebel group, hoping to enact change in the nation through cyberwarfare, or, they could be from, or employed, by a foreign nation poking at our defences, before disabling them!"[/i]
After Zorić little outburst, he takes a minute to collect himself, and turns towards the Premier, ensuring to take a more calm demeanour.
[i]"Sir, I believe we simply don't have the resources, or expertise, at our disposal to bring our cybersecurity to a sufficient level. We need to outsource..."[/i]

Rather quickly, the room would erupt into an incoherent rabble, as each minister begins to talk over each other, the tone of the room getting louder and louder.
With a simple gesture of raising his hand, the room, once again, falls into silence.
[i]"I would like to hear what he has to say."[/i] Premier Despotović would say, the rest of the ministers daring not to defy him.

[i]"Thank you, sir. Obviously, this whole ordeal needs to stay as hush-hush as it possibly can be. State Security will make sure of that. As for outsourcing... We've heard of the brief conflict that occurred on the west coast of Elseyr. Well, a private military company called SummitONE played a substantial role in turning the tide against the aggressor. I took liberty to do some digging around, and although they're based in High Albany, they're very reputable. I believe we can trust them to provide us cybersecurity, while they train up a cybersecurity team competent enough to safeguard us, and keep this whole ordeal quiet too. This sounds unreasonable, yes, but I be-"[/i]

Minister Zorić is interrupted by the Premier, who simply says. [i]"Very well. See to it."[/i]

Pleased with the Premiers willingness, the interior minister smiles, and the meeting continues for some time

Later that day...
An email is sent to the business email of SummitONE, along with a letter addressed to their headquarters in Stormhaven, Norrhollow, High Albany.
Inside the letter would be 6 "Access Permits". The summary of these access permits seem to indicate the holder of these permits grant access into the borders of the Slavaryian State. At the top of these permits, the coat of arms of the Slavaryian State is stamped onto the sheet, and at the bottom are two signatures, one from the Minister of Admission, and the other from the Minister of Internal Affairs.

Both the contents of the letter and the email appear to be identical, and appear to be for Xavier's eyes only. It reads as follows:
[i][b]"To Xavier Almstedt

Salutations Xavier Almstedt.

I sincerely hope this message finds you in good health. Allow me to introduce myself.
My name is Stanoje Zorić, and I am the Minister of Internal Affairs for the Slavaryian State.
My government has heard quite a lot about your remarkable company, and its involvement in recent events. I would like to express, on behalf of the National Authority of the Slavaryian State, my deepest admiration, and awe, to you, and your company, Mr Almstedt.

Now, as for why I am contacting you, it is the hope of the Slavaryian government that we may employ the services of SummitONE, particularly in the field of cybersecurity, and the potential training of cybersecurity staff.
I cordially invite a SummitONE business delegation to the Slavaryian capital of Slakovets, preferably within the boundaries of a few days to a week, to discuss this potential business relationship.

Within the letter that has been dispatched to your company headquarters are 6 special access permits.
6 individuals of the assigned business delegation will be permitted access to Slavaryian territory, providing they hold these permits as proof of invitation. 
Please note, these access permits are set to expire on the 01/05/2025.

It is assumed that your delegation will arrive by plane, and will be granted permission to land in Slakovets Tito National Airport.
If alternate method of transportation is more to your suiting, such as by boat, please respond to this email so that appropriate measures can be taken.
It should go without saying, but contraband such as explosives, firearms, and addictive narcotics are prohibited.

We look forward to doing business with you.
Sincerely,
Stanoje Zorić
Minister of Internal Affairs
Slavaryian State"
